summary: Internal SE/AE enablement focused on messaging, competitive positioning, and practicing the demo flows. Covered talking points for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, common customer objections (latency vs cost, data residency, SOC2/KMS), and a 2-run demo rehearsal with coaching notes.
topics: Security and compliance talking points (SOC2, SSO, KMS, VPC)
transcript:
[00:00] Meeting header: 2026-04-02 15:00 UTC, Duration 60m, Attendees: Ava Chen (AE), Liam Patel (SE), Jordan Rivera (PMM), Maya Gupta (CSM), Remy Ortiz, Priya Singh, Tom Brooks
[00:12] Ava Chen: All right, folks thanks for joining, quick agenda: update on messaging, competitor one-liners, and then two demo practice runs with feedback.
[00:28] Liam Patel: Quick note - we'll do Hosted first then Dedicated, and highlight when you'd pick Private.
[00:45] Jordan Rivera: I updated the one-pager with the new cost/latency bullets, link in chat after the call.
[01:10] Remy Ortiz: Cool, can we land on a single sentence for engineering folks? they want something short.
[01:22] Ava Chen: Yes, led with: "Redwood gives predictable inference economics with production-grade latency and unified tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." Short follow-ups: "Pin model versions, auto-fallbacks, and cost controls."
[01:45] Priya Singh: We should emphasize observability; platform teams will care about traces and token-level cost.
[02:02] Maya Gupta: Add that we have rollout policies and automatic fallback to compatible variants - that's a strong reliability hook.
[02:30] Tom Brooks: Competitors question: how do we compare to OpenAI on latency and cost?
[02:40] Liam Patel: Short answer: OpenAI has managed latency but limited deployment options; Redwood gives more control—dedicated pools for predictable throughput and private deployments for data residency. For cost, our batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations often win in unit economics for heavy production workloads.
[03:12] Jordan Rivera: Add rebuttal for Anthropic: they focus on safety/LLM models, but we win on serving controls and deployment flexibility; for Bedrock call out vendor lock-in risks and inconsistent SLAs.
[03:40] Ava Chen: Good, include an explicit line: "If they care about SSO, audit logs, and KMS control, Redwood supports private deployments, SOC2, and integrations with enterprise KMS/HSM."
[04:01] Liam Patel: Ok demo notes: Start with a quick 60s problem statement, then show the hosted API call (streaming), then flip to Redwood Dedicated dashboard for throughput SLOs and allocation, then mention Private (VPC) as the enterprise path.
[04:35] Remy Ortiz: Should we show a benchmark? customers always ask for numbers.
[04:45] Jordan Rivera: Yes show a simple table: hosted median latency 60-120ms for chat at 1k tokens/min workload, dedicated 30-70ms under reserved capacity; those are approximate, caveat language required.
[05:12] Priya Singh: Make sure to call out per-token cost drivers and tradeoffs with quantization.
[05:25] Liam Patel: Demo practice run 1: I'll narrate, Ava play the skeptical customer, Jordan will time and note points.
[05:40] [DEMO START]
[06:00] Liam Patel: Hi - thanks for meeting. We're looking at serving LLMs at scale, uncertain about cost and latency. Here's how Redwood approaches it: unified API, dedicated pools, and smart batching.
[06:20] Ava Chen (as customer): What's the difference between dedicated and hosted? do I get same model?
[06:30] Liam Patel: Yes, same model catalog, but dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput; hosted is best for quick time-to-value. If you need VPC or KMS we move to Private.
[07:00] Ava Chen: Our security team insists on SSO and audit logs, and some PII stays in requests.
[07:12] Liam Patel: We support RBAC, SAML/SSO, audit logs, and KMS integrations. For sensitive data we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS or on-prem option.
[07:40] Jordan Rivera: Note: call out SOC2 compliance and mention we have enterprise packs for retention settings.
[08:00] Ava Chen: What's the failover story if capacity spikes?
[08:12] Liam Patel: Smart routing and automated fallbacks - requests can route to a compatible model variant or different region; we also support burst capacity in Dedicated.
[08:35] [DEMO STOP]
[09:00] Maya Gupta: Feedback: quicker transitions, call out metrics upfront. Jordan: highlight observability console earlier.
[09:20] Liam Patel: Demo practice run 2 - I'll speed up and include a short benchmark slide.
[09:35] [DEMO START 2]
[09:55] Liam Patel: Quick problem statement, then show code snippet calling the Redwood API, streaming response, then switch to console to show token-level cost and per-route latency tracing.
[10:20] Ava Chen (as customer): Show me what dedicated looks like in the console.
[10:27] Liam Patel: (shares screen) here's Dedicated pools, autoscale policies, and SLA metrics. Notice the throughput graph and ability to pin model versions and set canary rollouts.
[10:55] Priya Singh: Nice, can we demo KV cache saving tokens on repeated prefixes?
[11:05] Liam Patel: Yes show a before/after cost estimate; that's a great callout for cost-sensitive apps.
[11:30] Remy Ortiz: Customer objection practice: latency vs accuracy tradeoff - they may want to quantize heavily.
[11:40] Jordan Rivera: Rebuttal: recommend targeted quantization profiles and guard rails, and suggest running a small A/B to validate quality before sweeping quantization.
[12:02] Ava Chen: Also prep answers for procurement: how long to onboard Dedicated and what's the commitment?
[12:12] Liam Patel: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 2-4 weeks for reserved pools; procurement asks are SLA, support tiers, and data residency.
[12:30] Maya Gupta: Add standard language for legal: we support DPA, SOC2, and can provide audit logs with Private.
[12:50] Jordan Rivera: Competitor script - short lines: OpenAI = fastest to prototype; Redwood = production economics + flexible deployment; Bedrock = vendor-backed catalog but inconsistent performance; Anthropic = model-focused safety, less on serving infra.
[13:20] Remy Ortiz: Good. Let's practice objection handling for price: customer says "your per-token cost is higher".
[13:30] Liam Patel: Rebuttal: total cost of ownership matters—beyond per-token, include developer time, SLA risks, and ability to optimize with batching and KV cache; offer pilot to show modeled savings.
[14:00] Ava Chen: Action item - record two demo runs and capture timestamps for each talking point.
[14:12] Liam Patel: I'll record and upload. Jordan will annotate.
[14:30] Maya Gupta: Also collect a quick FAQ for sales reps from this session.
[14:40] Jordan Rivera: I'll add sample email templates for follow-up including security docs links.
[15:00] [wrap-up] Recap of next steps and owners.
[15:20] Ava Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and recording. End meeting.
